items.title: Flag-variety twisted differential operators and their modules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the published group and sheaf suppliers. Let $G$ be a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine algebraic group, $B\supseteq T$ a Borel subgroup and maximal torus, $X=G/B$, $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}G$, $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}T$, and $\Phi^+$ the positive roots selected by $B$. Write $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. All schemes are over $\mathbb C$. For an integral weight $\eta$, $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ denotes the $G$-equivariant line bundle $G\times^B\mathbb C_\eta$ with fiber character $\eta$ at $eB$. The infinitesimal $G$-action gives an anchor $$a_X:\mathcal L_X:=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g\longrightarrow T_X,\qquad f\otimes x\longmapsto f x_X.$$ Give $\mathcal L_X$ the action-algebroid bracket $$[f\otimes x,g\otimes y]=fg\otimes[x,y]+f x_X(g)\otimes y-g y_X(f)\otimes x.$$ Its kernel $\mathfrak b_X=\ker a_X$ is the isotropy Lie-algebra bundle; at $gB$ its fiber is $\operatorname{Ad}(g)\mathfrak b$. For any $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, the character $\kappa+\rho$ of $\mathfrak b$ (zero on $\mathfrak n^+$) transports to an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}:\mathfrak b_X\to\mathcal O_X$. The transport is independent of the representative $g$ of $gB$, since a character is invariant under the adjoint action of $B$. The action-algebroid enveloping sheaf $\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by $\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal L_X$ with the displayed bracket and $$[x,f]=x_X(f),\qquad x\in\mathcal L_X,\ f\in\mathcal O_X.$$ Define the sheaf of twisted differential operators $$\mathcal D_\kappa:=\mathcal U_X(\mathfrak g)/\bigl(\xi-\chi^X_{\kappa+\rho}(\xi):\xi\in\mathfrak b_X\bigr).$$ Its order filtration assigns order zero to $\mathcal O_X$ and order at most one to the image of $\mathcal L_X$. A TDO means a filtered $\mathcal O_X$-ring with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$, associated graded $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X$, and first-order commutator equal to the anchor; the well-definedness and PBW properties of $\mathcal D_\kappa$ are proved in [[lem-pa36-flag-tdo-pbw-and-twist]]. A left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module below is required to be quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal O_X$-module. For $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, let $\operatorname{pr}(z)\in U(\mathfrak h)$ be the Harish–Chandra projection along the chosen triangular decomposition, and put $$\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho).$$ This is the shifted central character: the Harish–Chandra isomorphism makes it $W$-invariant in $\kappa$. Define $$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa.$$ The regularity convention is **antidominant** when $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\notin\mathbb Z_{>0}$ for each positive root $\alpha$, and **regular** when $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ne0$ for every root. For complex weights, $\mathbb Z_{>0}$ means the positive real integers; no order on arbitrary complex numbers is used.

items.title: Global sections on module sheaves have ordinary sheaf cohomology as derived functors
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathscr A)$ be a topological space with a sheaf of unital rings (not necessarily commutative), and let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)$ be the category of sheaves of left $\mathscr A$-modules. Then this category has enough injectives, every injective $\mathscr A$-module sheaf is flasque as an underlying sheaf of abelian groups, and for every $\mathscr A$-module sheaf $M$ the right-derived functors of global sections in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)$ satisfy $$R^q\Gamma_{\operatorname{Mod}(\mathscr A)}(X,M) \cong H^q(X,M)\qquad(q\ge0),$$ where the right side is ordinary sheaf cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf.

items.title: Cech cohomology of line bundles on the projective line
items.statement: For $d\in\mathbb Z$, let $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)$ have standard frames $e_0,e_1$ on $U_0=\{x\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{y\ne0\}$ with $e_1=z^d e_0$ on the overlap, where $z=y/x$ and $w=1/z$. Then $$\dim H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(d+1,0),\qquad \dim H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(d))=\max(-d-1,0),$$ and $H^q=0$ for $q\ge2$. For $d\ge0$, the global sections on $U_0$ are the polynomials of degree at most $d$; for $d\le-2$, $H^1$ has Laurent basis $z^{d+1},z^{d+2},\ldots,z^{-1}$.

items.title: The principal nilpotent Borel orbit by height elimination
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and the setup of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]. For each simple root $\alpha_i$ choose a nonzero root vector $e_i\in\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$ and put $e=\sum_i e_i$. Write $\mathfrak n^+_j=\bigoplus_{\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)=j}\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Then $$B\cdot e=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}c_\alpha e_\alpha\in\mathfrak n^+: c_{\alpha_i}\ne0\text{ for every simple root }\alpha_i\right\},$$ where one nonzero $e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is fixed for each positive root. The right side is independent of the choices of those root vectors.

items.title: Quasicoherent modules are filtered unions of coherent subsheaves and cohomology commutes with these colimits
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=G/B$ be the projective flag variety of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]], and let $\mathcal M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Then $\mathcal M$ is the filtered union of its coherent $\mathcal O_X$-submodules. If $\mathcal M=\varinjlim_j\mathcal F_j$ is any filtered colimit of quasi-coherent modules, then for every $q\ge0$ the canonical map $$\varinjlim_j H^q(X,\mathcal F_j)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal M)$$ is an isomorphism.

items.title: PBW and integral line-bundle twisting for flag TDOs
items.statement: Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying $$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$ If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then $$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$ and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

items.title: Normality of the nilpotent cone and Springer functions
items.statement: Assume the setup of [[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]] and the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be the nilpotent cone with its reduced coordinate ring from [[lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-reduced-integral-domain]], and let $\mu:T^*X\to N$ be the Springer moment map. Then $N$ is normal, $\mu$ is proper and birational, and pullback induces a graded algebra isomorphism $$\mathbb C[N]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T^*X,\mathcal O_{T^*X}).$$

items.title: Partial-flag twist and local product decomposition
Global sections of twisted differential operators on the flag variety
items.statement: Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]] and the Axiom of Choice. For every complex $\kappa$, the infinitesimal action on $\mathcal D_\kappa$ induces a filtered algebra isomorphism $$A_\kappa=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\kappa \xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_\kappa),$$ where $\chi_\kappa(z)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\kappa-\rho)$. No dominance, regularity, or integrality condition is imposed on $\kappa$.

items.title: Global sections and localization at a fixed infinitesimal character
items.statement: Fix $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ and $A_\kappa$, $\mathcal D_\kappa$ as in [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. By [[thm-pa36-global-twisted-differential-operators]], the sheaf $\mathcal D_\kappa$ is a right $A_\kappa$-module by multiplication by global sections, and $\Gamma(X,-)$ takes values in left $A_\kappa$-modules through the infinitesimal action. Define $$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa(V):=\mathcal D_\kappa\otimes_{A_\kappa}V, \qquad V\in A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},$$ where the tensor product is the sheaf tensor product. Define $\Gamma_\kappa(M):=\Gamma(X,M)$ for a quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$. Localization is right exact as a tensor functor. The next item proves the adjunction and verifies that these constructions land in the stated categories.

items.title: Ample translation maps split by central-character separation
items.statement: Let $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ and let $\eta$ be a sufficiently dominant integral weight, so that $L_\eta=\mathcal O_X(-\eta)$ is ample. Put $V_\eta=\Gamma(X,L_\eta)^*$, the finite-dimensional irreducible representation of highest weight $\eta$. For any quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$, the natural coevaluation map $$M\longrightarrow M\otimes L_\eta\otimes V_\eta$$ is a split injection of action-algebroid modules when $\kappa$ is antidominant. The natural evaluation map $$M\otimes V_\eta^*\longrightarrow M\otimes L_\eta$$ is a split surjection of action-algebroid modules when $\kappa$ is regular antidominant. The tensor products in these two statements carry the diagonal infinitesimal $\mathfrak g$-action and the corresponding $B$-linearization.

items.title: Localization is left adjoint to global sections
items.statement: For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$, $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to \operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)$ is left adjoint to $\Gamma_\kappa:\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)\to A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$.

items.title: Antidominant twists are D-affine and regular ones are conservative
items.statement: Assume the flag-variety setup of [[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. If $\kappa$ is antidominant, then every quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$ satisfies $$H^i(X,M)=0\qquad(i>0).$$ If $\kappa$ is also regular, then $\Gamma(X,M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The antidominance and regularity conditions are independent hypotheses; regularity alone does not imply the vanishing assertion.

items.title: The unit V to Gamma Loc_kappa(V) is an isomorphism for antidominant twists
items.statement: For antidominant $\kappa$ and every left $A_\kappa$-module $V$, the unit of the adjunction in [[lem-pa36-localization-adjunction]] is an isomorphism $$V\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa V).$$

items.title: The singular simple-parabolic kernel on the flag variety
items.statement: Let $\kappa$ be antidominant and let $\alpha$ be a simple root with $\langle\kappa,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$. Put $p_\alpha:X=G/B\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$, a Zariski-locally trivial $\mathbb P^1$-bundle, and let $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\beta\in\Phi^+}\beta$. Use the partial TDO $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$ and pullback module $p_\alpha^\dagger N$ defined in [[lem-pa36-partial-flag-twist-product]]. For every coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$: 1. $R^q p_{\alpha*}M=0$ for every $q>0$; 2. $p_{\alpha*}M=0$ if and only if there is a unique coherent $\mathcal D^{\alpha}_{\kappa-\rho}$-module $N$ with $$M\cong\mathcal O_X(\rho)\otimes p_\alpha^\dagger N,$$ where $N\cong p_{\alpha*}(\mathcal O_X(-\rho)\otimes M)$. The proof below establishes the forward implication in (2) and reduces the reverse implication to an explicit rank-one kernel classification; that classification remains escalated and is not treated as proved here.

items.title: The singular antidominant Serre quotient
items.statement: Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, not necessarily regular, and let $$\Gamma=\Gamma_\kappa:\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa) \longrightarrow A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},\qquad K=\ker\Gamma.$$ Then $K$ is a Serre subcategory and the induced functors give an equivalence of abelian categories $$\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa)/K \simeq A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}.$$ The quotient has representatives precisely among the quasicoherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules that are generated by global sections and have no nonzero quasicoherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-submodule with zero global sections. No equivalence with the whole $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module category is asserted without regularity.

items.title: Regular antidominant Beilinson–Bernstein localization
items.statement: Assume the setup of [[def-pa36-global-sections-and-localization]]. If $\kappa$ is regular antidominant, then $$\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa:A_\kappa\text{-}\mathbf{Mod} \rightleftarrows\operatorname{QCoh}(X,\mathcal D_\kappa):\Gamma_\kappa$$ are inverse equivalences between all left $A_\kappa$-modules and all quasi-coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. The equivalence restricts to finitely generated $A_\kappa$-modules and coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules. It does not assert that $\Gamma$ is faithful for a fixed non-antidominant representative of a regular central character. Here a coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module means a module locally finitely presented over the sheaf of rings $\mathcal D_\kappa$; its local noetherianity is part of the proof below.

items.title: The integral regular localization equivalence restricts to Category O
items.statement: Let $\kappa$ be integral, regular and antidominant. Define the **exact central-character subcategory** $$\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}} =\{V\in\mathcal O:(\ker\chi_\kappa)V=0\}.$$ A **strongly $B$-equivariant coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module** means a coherent left $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module with a rational $B$-linearization whose differential is the action-algebroid action and whose action is compatible with the $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module structure. Then $\operatorname{Loc}_\kappa$ and $\Gamma_\kappa$ restrict to inverse equivalences between $\mathcal O_{\chi_\kappa}^{\mathrm{exact}}$ and these strongly $B$-equivariant coherent modules. The exact subcategory is distinct from the generalized-character block, where each vector is killed by some power of $\ker\chi_\kappa$; the theorem does not identify the whole generalized block with $B$-equivariant coherent modules.

items.title: Kashiwara's singular parabolic kernel filtration
items.statement: Let $\kappa$ be antidominant, let $$J=\{\alpha_i\in\Delta:\langle\kappa,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\},$$ and assume its full zero-root subsystem is generated by $J$. For each $\alpha\in J$, write $p_\alpha:X\to X_\alpha=G/P_\alpha$ for the simple parabolic projection. Then there exists a finite sequence $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N\in J$ such that for every coherent $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module $M$ the following are equivalent: 1. $\Gamma(X,M)=0$; 2. there is a finite coherent filtration $$M=M_0\supseteq M_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq M_N=0$$ with $p_{\alpha_j*}(M_{j-1}/M_j)=0$ for every $j$. The sequence is one choice, not asserted to be unique. The proof below gives the sequence and proves (2)$\Rightarrow$(1); its converse is escalated because it requires the rank-one kernel supplier [[lem-pa36-singular-parabolic-kernel]].

title: Beilinson–Bernstein Localization and Category O: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A positive integral SL2 twist is regular but not D-affine
items.statement: Regularity of $\kappa$ alone implies that $\Gamma(X,-)$ is exact and conservative for $\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules.

items.title: The SL2 flag charts realize the stated rho shift
items.statement: Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)$, $X=G/B\cong\mathbb P^1$, and use the repository basis $$h=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad e=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ Let $\rho$ satisfy $\rho(h)=1$. For an integer $c$, set $\kappa=c\rho$ and $d=-c-1$. Then $$\mathcal D_{c\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(d)).$$ On $U_0=\{x\ne0\}$ with coordinate $z=y/x$ and frame $e_0=x^d$, the infinitesimal action is $$e=z^2\partial_z+(c+1)z,\qquad f=-\partial_z,\qquad h=2z\partial_z+(c+1).$$ On $U_1=\{y\ne0\}$ with coordinate $w=x/y$ and frame $e_1=y^d$, it is $$e=-\partial_w,\qquad f=w^2\partial_w+(c+1)w,\qquad h=-2w\partial_w-(c+1).$$ These formulas glue, satisfy the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations, and give $\mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1})$ when $c=-1$.

items.title: Integral line-bundle translation changes the infinitesimal character
items.statement: For $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$, start at the singular twist $\kappa=0$ with the nonzero $\mathcal D_0$-module $M=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. Tensor by the integral line bundle $\mathcal O_X(\rho)=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)$. The result is the $\mathcal D_\rho$-module $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-2)$, since integral line-bundle translation changes the twist from $\kappa$ to $\kappa+\rho$. The Casimir characters change from $$\chi_0(C)=-\tfrac12\quad\text{to}\quad\chi_\rho(C)=0.$$ The translated parameter $\rho$ is not antidominant, and the translated module still has zero global sections (indeed $\dim H^1=1$); the twist equivalence on sheaf modules does not assert that global sections is faithful at the translated parameter.

items.title: A point-supported SL2 module gives the shifted Verma module
items.statement: Use $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$, $X=\mathbb P^1$, and $\kappa=c\rho$ with $c\in\mathbb Z$. Let $x_0$ be the Borel-fixed point $z=0$ in the $U_0$ chart of [[ex-pa36-sl2-twisted-differential-operators]], and let $\delta_{x_0}$ be the left $\mathcal D_{c\rho}$-module supported at $x_0$. Then $$\Gamma(X,\delta_{x_0})\cong M((c-1)\rho)=U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_{(c-1)\rho}.$$ For the Casimir $$C=ef+fe+\tfrac12h^2,$$ both this Verma module and the central character $\chi_{c\rho}$ have scalar $\frac12(c^2-1)$.

items.title: At the singular SL2 twist global sections is not conservative
items.statement: The global-sections functor is conservative for every antidominant twist, including singular twists, and the corresponding simple-parabolic pushforward detects every nonzero module.

items.title: Finite-dimensional sl2 modules lie in the exact integral central-character part
items.statement: Let $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ and $n\ge0$. The finite-dimensional irreducible $V(n\rho)$ of highest weight $n\rho$ lies in BGG category $\mathcal O$ and has exact central character $\chi_{(n+1)\rho}$. Since the Weyl group sends $(n+1)\rho$ to $-(n+1)\rho$, the same character has regular antidominant representative $$\kappa=-(n+1)\rho.$$ The corollary [[cor-pa36-category-o-localization]] therefore localizes this object to a coherent strongly B-equivariant $\mathcal D_\kappa$-module. The claim concerns the **exact** central-character subcategory $\ker\chi_\kappa\cdot V=0$. The generalized-character condition $\forall v\ \exists N:\,(\ker\chi_\kappa)^N v=0$ is a different condition; no equivalence for the entire generalized block is asserted.
